dedupe_keys.name: modelica co simulation variants for emissions and cost reduction in sustainable district heating planning

description: This record describes a Modelica-based modelling study, posted as an arXiv preprint in 2025 by the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology, that introduces a methodology for variant analysis in future district heating planning, aiming to optimise emissions and costs. Models of the heating centre, heat grid pipelines and heating interface units to buildings are coupled in co-simulations, which allow a comparative analysis of economic feasibility and sustainability for different technologies and energy carriers. A new modular, highly parameterizable building model serves to validate the introduced heat grid model. The results reported in the abstract are that bio-methane cuts carbon equivalent emissions by nearly 70 percent relative to conventional natural gas heating, hydrogen with a heat pump cuts them by 77 percent, and ground source heat pumps show high economic viability. Coverage is a residential district heating case in Germany. Access: the paper is on arXiv, free; no code repository or licence is stated on the pages read. Caveats: results concern the modelled residential area and cost assumptions in the paper. It suits early-stage district heating design comparisons, and no directly related records are catalogued yet.
